prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1054; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver's side rear quarter panel. Claimant reports driver was transported by ambulance from the scene and diagnosed with a concussion. Liability questions noted for review. Claimant is not represented by counsel at this time.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports headaches, light sensitivity, and dizziness since the collision and has been advised to follow up with a treating physician. Claimant provided photos of vehicle damage and the medical discharge summary. Explained the claims process and that claimant may choose to consult an attorney at any time. No settlement discussed.

Entry 3: Obtained the insured's recorded statement. Insured states they checked the mirror and signaled before moving left but did not see the claimant's vehicle in the adjacent lane. Insured acknowledges contact occurred during the lane change. Insured's account is consistent with the initial report. Photos of insured vehicle damage received and added to file.

Entry 4: Requested the scene report and any available dashcam footage from both parties. Claimant states a witness in a nearby vehicle stopped to assist and left contact information, which has been requested. Reviewed the photos and estimate for the claimant's vehicle. Repair estimate received and under review. Medical records authorization sent to claimant for the treating facility.

Entry 5: Received medical records confirming concussion diagnosis and recommended follow-up care. Claimant's treating provider has placed the claimant on a period of restricted activity. Liability assessment in progress, leaning toward insured responsibility given the lane change circumstances. File flagged for supervisor review before any offer is made. Follow-up scheduled with claimant to confirm status.
